# evroc_loadbalancer (Resource)

Provides an evroc Layer 4 (TCP) load balancer resource for distributing traffic across backend targets.


If `backend_network` is omitted, the load balancer attaches to the default VPC
and the default subnet in every zone. For backend VMs in a custom VPC, configure
that VPC and its subnets explicitly. The load balancer deploys only to zones with
a configured subnet. Backend networking is immutable; adding, changing, or
removing this block replaces the load balancer.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "evroc_loadbalancer" "cluster" {
  name          = "my-lb"
  public_ip_ref = evroc_public_ip.vip.fqid

  backend_network {
    vpc_ref = evroc_vpc.cluster.fqid

    subnet {
      zone       = "a"
      subnet_ref = evroc_subnet.cluster["a"].fqid
    }
    subnet {
      zone       = "b"
      subnet_ref = evroc_subnet.cluster["b"].fqid
    }
  }

  listener {
    name       = "supervisor"
    protocol   = "TCP"
    port       = 9345
    route_refs = [evroc_lb_l4_route.supervisor.fqid]
  }
}
```

## Import and migration

Import an existing load balancer using its name, with the provider configured for
its project and region:

```shell
terraform import evroc_loadbalancer.cluster my-lb
```

For a load balancer previously created through the CLI with `--vpc` and `--subnet`,
add a matching `backend_network` block before applying with a provider version
that supports it. Read/import populates the block from the API; omitting it from
configuration proposes replacement to restore the default networking. If the
load balancer is already in Terraform state, refresh it with `terraform plan`
instead of importing it again. Review the plan before applying.

An existing load balancer attached to the wrong VPC must be replaced; upgrading
the provider alone does not fix its network. Schedule the replacement for an
appropriate maintenance window and retain the existing public IP resource if the
address must stay the same.

## Schema

### Required

- `listener` (Block Set, Min: 1) List of listeners (port mappings) for the load balancer. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--listener))
- `name` (String) Name of the load balancer. Must be unique within the project. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `public_ip_ref` (String) Fully qualified reference to the public IP for the load balancer (e.g., evroc_public_ip.my_ip.fqid). Changing this forces a new resource to be created.

### Optional

- `backend_network` (Block List, Max: 1) VPC and subnets for reaching backend VMs. If omitted, the load balancer attaches to the default VPC in every zone. When specified, the load balancer deploys only to the zones with a configured subnet. Changing this forces a new resource to be created. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--backend_network))
- `project` (String) Project this resource belongs to. Defaults to the provider project. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `region` (String) Region where the load balancer is created. Defaults to provider region. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `user_labels` (Map of String) User-defined labels (key/value pairs) for organizing and selecting resources.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Timestamp when the load balancer was created (RFC3339 format).
- `fqid` (String) Fully qualified resource ID (FQID). Use this to reference this resource from other resources.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `lb_id` (String) Unique identifier (UUID) of the load balancer.
- `public_ipv4_address` (String) Assigned public IPv4 address of the load balancer.
- `system_labels` (Map of String) System-managed labels automatically set by evroc (read-only).

<a id="nestedblock--backend_network"></a>
### Nested Schema for `backend_network`

Required:

- `vpc_ref` (String) Fully qualified reference to the VPC containing the backend VMs. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `subnet` (Block Set, Min: 1) Subnets to attach to in the selected VPC, with one subnet per deployment zone. Changing this forces a new resource to be created. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--backend_network--subnet))

<a id="nestedblock--backend_network--subnet"></a>
### Nested Schema for `backend_network.subnet`

Required:

- `zone` (String) Zone to deploy to: a, b, or c. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `subnet_ref` (String) Fully qualified reference to the subnet in this zone. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.


<a id="nestedblock--listener"></a>
### Nested Schema for `listener`

Required:

- `port` (Number) Frontend port that the load balancer listens on.
- `protocol` (String) Protocol for the listener. Currently only 'TCP' is supported.
- `route_refs` (Set of String) Set of fully qualified L4 route references (e.g., evroc_lb_l4_route.my_route.fqid).

Optional:

- `name` (String) Name for this listener (e.g., 'web', 'api'). Must be unique per load balancer.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String)
- `delete` (String)
- `update` (String)
